title: Choose the visual world
question: Built around your steer: a dotted route down through illustrated, animated layers. The roll assigned The Wall Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Wall Chart
options.lineage: hand-coloured classroom wall charts of the Earth's cross-section
options.thesis: A saturated classroom cutaway of the Earth, with a traveller's dotted route descending through every illustrated layer.
materials: linen-backed sheet with a title cartouche
options.viewport: Everest drawn huge in hachure against a Prussian-blue sky, snow streaming off the summit, the dotted route starting at a flag marked 8,849 m.
options.risk: Antique charts drift to parchment and quaint; it must stay saturated and animated or it becomes a museum reproduction.

raised.raise: The route is one continuous hand-drawn curve that sets the page's composition, not a grid of boxes.
Every layer has its own living weather: spindrift on Everest, slow convection in the mantle, molten iron streaming in the outer core.
A traveller marker rides the dotted line and always shows where you are, with depth and temperature on its tag.
Every illustration prints from one fixed set of seven inks; a gap in the outline prints as an empty ruled box.

options.label: The Park Trail Map
options.thesis: The descent as one illustrated trail: numbered trail markers, painted terrain, a red dotted path from the summit to the core.
options.viewport: A painted Everest with snow blowing across it, a carved sign reading 'Summit · 8,849 m', the red trail dropping toward Camp 1.
options.risk: The closest to what most runs would make once a map was asked for.

options.label: Living Shader Descent
options.thesis: Each layer is a full-screen living shader, a blizzard or a molten flow, with the route drawn over it.
options.viewport: A full-screen blizzard shader parting around the cursor, one word, SUMMIT, oversized, the dotted route a thin line through it.
options.case: Holds audience identification (immersive and game-like) but loses clarity: thin type over moving pixels is hard to read, and the route becomes an overlay.
options.risk: Heavy GPU work on a classroom laptop; the map stops being the structure.

options.label: Curved-Crease Shell
options.thesis: One arc folds a flat sheet into a shell.
options.viewport: A folded disc on a compass arc.
options.case: Declined: no geology in a paper fold.
options.kept: One sweeping curve rules the layout.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.thesis: Districts fold like quilts, each dreaming its own weather.
options.case: Declined: dreamy surrealism blurs the science.
options.kept: Each region carries its own living weather.

options.label: Drum Machine Steps
options.thesis: Layers as sixteen steps under a chase light.
options.case: Declined: an instrument costume for a geology walk.
options.kept: A marker always shows where 'now' is.

options.label: Kiosk Print
options.thesis: Layers as matchbox labels in three inks.
options.case: Declined: a grid can't carry a descent.
options.kept: A fixed ink set; gaps print as empty boxes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The classic 'journey to the center' scroll story, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A night-sky Everest silhouette, a big title, and a depth meter pinned to the side.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every Earth-layers explainer on the web.
